campaign.description: In which the new settlers come to understand the severity of their situation.

beats.label: Thatwards Ho!
beats.description:
“Operation: Go, And It Take” (or: “Go, On Them Tread”) 

A Beginner Scenario for the Frontier Formerly Known As Texas 

All right, so here’s the deal, folks.You’ve been voluntold—uh, selected—to go Thatwards. 

Yes, Thatwards. 

Look, the cardinal directions didn’t survive the Shattering. Now the world uses the Nine Directional Qualia: 

Yonder 
Thither 
Overwhere 
Up Shit Creek 
Timbuktu 
Ass Backwards 
Edgewards 
Nowherenohow 
…and Thatwards (where you’re going!) 

You’re being sent to the Frontier Formerly Known As Texas, a region we think used to be Texas because: 

The maps say it was Texas. 

The terrain looks vaguely Texan. 

People around here know the legends of Whataburger, Buc-ee’s, and Borderline Irrational State Pride. 

Also, the Akashic field hiccups whenever someone says “Remember the Alamo,” so something traumatic clearly happened. 

The world is dark. Almost Qliphothic levels of “please stop hitting yourselves,”and violence?

Violence now breaks reality even harder than Texas state politics used to. 

The Good News? Even the worst enemies on the continent have realized that if everyone keeps shooting laser-dragons at each other, the vacuum of mutually assured self-enweirdment will collapse the very notion of linear time. So congratulations—diplomacy is mandatory now!

(Or at least cruelty-optional.) 

So what are you actually DOING here? 

Somewhere near your new holdings, supposedly, there is an old bunker. An ancient pre-Shattering bolt-hole of untold significance. 

Rumors say it contains: 

lost infrastructure tech, 
old-world terraforming systems, 
pre-civilizational Spark-related artifacts (could be Vestigial), 
or just a crate of MREs and a semi-functional 3D printer. 

Honestly, who knows. 

But your coalition wants it. Which means other definitely want it too and probably shouldn't have it. 

And the Valhaulans—the Techno-Viking Pirate Raiders and knot belayers extraordinaire—already live inside it and have declared the bunker their “Rightful Sacred Battle-Bassinet.”

Not great. 

THIS is where you come in.

You’re “expendable but promising.” You genuinely seem like the sort of weirdos reality wants to survive. Which is why you're here. You've already got a pretty big fan! 

So - your jobs: 

1 - Claim and cleanse hexes in cooperation with, not opposition to, those you find there. Darkness begets darkness in very literal ways here, where the pathways of the mind still run dark and strong. 

2 - Identify Sparks 

3 - Make friends with new factions 

4 - Melt Qlipothic things' faces

5 - Have fun!

beats.label: Allesh-Gilliam - Welcome!
beats.description:
The road ends without ceremony. The Jackalope transport rattles to a stop like it’s tired of pretending this was optional. You're in charge here now. In theory, inanimate objects do what YOU say. NOT the other way around. You're sure of this. Probably.

Dust rolls in slow, deliberate waves. The air smells like hot metal, creosote, and old rain that never quite made it to the ground but sticks around in the most annoyingly humid way possible. Ahead, Allesh‑Gilliam rises from the wreckage of an East Texas town that refused to finish dying.

Walls made from overturned semis, refinery plate, welded storefronts, and the remains of water towers lean into each other like tired friends. Nothing matches. Everything works.

A hand‑painted sign hangs over the gate in a Circuitgraph:

ALLESH‑GILLIAM
HOLD FAST · PAY DEBTS · DON’T LIE TO THE LAND

The town exhales as you approach.

Something here has opinions.

beats.label: Avuncular Joans - Sendoff Speech

choices.label: Go To Allesh Gilliam Quest List

beats.description:
Avuncular Joan waits for you just inside the gate. Cloak dusted. Eyes tired in the way only responsibility can do. She looks past you for half a second—as if checking whether something followed you off the transport—and then smiles.

“All right,” she says. “This is where the theory ends.”

She gestures broadly: the town, the walls, the three hexes you now technically command.

“Allesh-Gilliam. Lyrenn. Khezek Tor.
A fortress, a farm, and a hole in the ground.
Together, they’re a promise.”

Her voice lowers.

“Bad Eden is not hostile because it hates you.
It’s hostile because it remembers being lied to.”

She presses a sigil into the air. The Leygate hums behind her—bright, restrained, clearly labeled EMERGENCIES ONLY by someone who meant it.

“I’ll be in Coraliindra.
You won’t see me unless something has gone very right…
or very wrong.”

A beat. A smile that doesn’t quite reach her eyes.

“Don’t try to save everything at once.
Start by keeping one promise.”

The Leygate flares.

She’s gone.

The gate closes.

The town exhales.

choices.label: HQ
choices.description:
So, ok, it's probably a good idea to check out your command center and new home. It used to be something called a "Snarky Burger," but now it's a highly efficient bunker filled with technology and, yes ok fine, old grease traps.

Marshal Yarrow Pike will meet you there. Hopefully he does not inquire about your desire to have fries with your new command.

choices.label: St Gilliam's
choices.description:
Time to go to church! Except given that religion has now been turned on its lack of gods-damned head, (you can apply to be a god now in certain hexes), churches aren't what they used to be. But the Order of the Holy Turnpike are good people. Father Tamsin has turned his abode into a bed and breakfast for those as are passing through.

So the dude knows ALL the dirt.

choices.label: The Long Market
choices.description:
Yes you have to pay for stuff here even though you are in charge. Most of what's available is standard issue though, so it's covered. Take a look!

That's also where you'll find Etta Bloom, the closest thing that Allesh-Gilliam has to a mayor. Which means not very close. But worth talking to.

beats.label: Allesh-Gilliam - HQ Cinematics
beats.description:
Once, this place sold burgers that apologized for themselves.

Now it sells certainty.

The cracked Snarky Burger sign still flickers outside, the mascot’s grin frozen mid‑sarcasm. Inside, the smell of old grease has been overtaken by ozone, dust, and warm circuitry. Booths have been torn out and replaced with map tables. The soda fountain is a coolant line now.

The old ordering menu boards glow to life when you enter.

Not combos anymore.

Hex readouts. Patrol routes. Leyline flow. Supply pressure. Soft‑warning colors that mean someone should look at this soon.

Someone repurposed nostalgia into infrastructure.

This is headquarters.

beats.label: Allesh-Gilliam - Visit Your New HQ

choices.label: Check out the East Wall
choices.description: So THAT sounded like a challenge. Pike seems fairly keen on being unimpressed. It would be awesome to make him impressed. Impress him, impress others more easily. Or at least piss them off less easily. Actually who knows I'm done making predictions.

choices.label: Head to the Leygate
choices.description: You've met the Jackalopes before. They're fine. Good in a pinch. Definitely good to stay on the good side of the merchants around here. Seeing one of their above ground Enclaves could be educational. But first, time to check out your busted ass equipment.

beats.description:
Marshal Yarrow Pike doesn’t stand when you enter. He leans against the counter like it’s the only thing in the room that hasn’t disappointed him yet.

Scar across the jaw. Eyes that measure distances automatically.

“All right,” he says. “You’re the new variable.”

He gestures at the glowing menu boards.

“That wall holds if people believe it will. That land feeds us if we don’t lie to it. And that gate?”

He taps a flickering leyline readout.

“That thing is remembering wrong.”

He finally looks directly at you.

“Fix one promise first. Then we’ll see how long you last. Fix two, well, maybe people might follow instead of holding their breath. Or measuring you for a box.

We need a replacement Leygate Stabilizer, and the only place I know that has one is Furrier's Fixit. Probably good you know them.

Also," he gestures at the maps again, and one section of city wall that stands out as … wrong.

See if you can tell us what we're doing wrong."

choices.label: Show us the wall that’s wrong. Um. Please.
Do you have an echo story?

beats.label: Allesh-Gilliam - Marshall Yarrow Convo, 1
beats.description:
Yarrow doesn’t bristle. That’s important.

“It flickered. We believed the previous report instead of the current signal.”

A pause.

“Belief killed timing.”

“You ever trust a system because it worked yesterday?”

He watches your answer like a entire firing line watching a potential victim.

beats.label: Allesh-Gilliam - Marshall Yarrow Convo, 2
beats.description:
He nods once.

No speech. Just walks you to the map.

“This section bows inward.”

He taps it.

“Architect says it's cosmetic.”

He waits.

beats.label: Allesh-Gilliam - Marshall Yarrow Convo, 3
beats.description:
“Pick something visible.”

“Finish it.”

“No speeches.”

He folds his arms.

“If people see follow-through once, they’ll lend you patience twice.”

beats.label: Allesh-Gilliam - Marshall Yarrow Convo, 4
beats.description:
A beat.

“No.”

Not hostile. Just factual.

“But I don’t distrust you either.”

“You’re unproven. That’s neutral.”

beats.label: Allesh-Gilliam - Marshall Yarrow, Echo
beats.description:
Yarrow doesn’t answer immediately.

He shifts his weight.

“Unfinished?”

A dry exhale.

“I was supposed to hold a gate once.”

His eyes drift to the leyline readout.

“It failed. Or I failed it. Depends how you write history.”

A long pause.

“People died because we trusted something that flickered.”

He looks at you without blinking.

“I think I’m here to see one promise actually hold.”

A beat.

“Just one. Clean. No hedging.”

His jaw tightens slightly.

“After that? Maybe I go quiet.”

beats.label: Allesh-Gilliam - Inspect The East Wall

choices.label: Reinforce structure properly
choices.description: You've heard legends of the game Jenga. You think you would have probably been good at it. Time to prove it! With several tons of corrugated steel and concrete.

choices.label: Rally workers and patrols
choices.description: What people around here is, like, a inspirational song or story about how a brave spoon full of sugar somehow made people better at work, and so they fixed a shitty wall. That's inspiration!

choices.label: Reassign patrols, predict pressure points
choices.description: Before you make the plan, you have to plan for making the plan. You want to do this right? SPY ON THE FUCKING WALL and it will tell you what it needs. Just don't let it know you're listening.

choices.label: Overbuild and intimidate the problem
choices.description: You know what? Fuck this wall. It seems ungrateful. Remind it that it was made out of a bunch of junk, and it's two seconds away from returning to that state unless it shapes up and gets its act together. There are PLENTY of walls that would KILL for a job like this. Would you kill for me, wall???

beats.description:
The East Wall smells like fresh weld and tired optimism.

Beyond it: scrub, wind, and things that do not respect fences.

On this side: people who would like to sleep tonight.

Scouts rotate constantly. Someone patched the same section twice already.

The wall is holding.

For now.

beats.label: Allesh-Gilliam East Wall Success
beats.description:
Making a good first impression is important. Making a good first impression that also shows that you know what you're doing? THAT means you won't be killed in your sleep by locals dissatisfied with leadership.

People are blunt here. Or sharp. Or grating. Or medical grade bone sawing.

beats.label: Allesh-Gilliam - East Wall Failure
beats.description:
Well. The less said about that the better.

Which is why I'm going to say - you only get so many swings and misses. Pick your battles. Stay in milk. Drink your drugs. Don't do school.

Am I making myself clear?

beats.label: Allesh-Gilliam - St Gilliam's Interior
beats.description:
Candles everywhere.

Not ceremonial. Practical.

Quiet agreements are made here. People say prayers even if they don’t believe anymore.

Some say the land listens more closely here than anywhere else in town.

beats.label: Allesh-Gilliam - Go To Church! (Intro to St Gilliam's)
beats.description:
Father Tamsin speaks softly, like raising his voice would scare something important away.

“There’s food,” he says. “There’s rest. And there’s a place to sit without being measured.”

He pauses, hands folded.

“Khezek Tor feeds the town. It also asks for more than it admits.”

A gentle look.

“Mountains remember how they’re treated.”

beats.label: Allesh-Gilliam - Father Tamsin Conversation

choices.label: You think Khezek Tor is angry?

beats.description:
Father Tamsin senses that you are curious. He folds his hands. And without prompting, tells you his echo story.

“I was a healer.”

A gentle tone.

“There was a night I chose who to save.”

No bitterness. No drama.

“Someone asked for mercy. I told myself there wasn’t enough.”

A pause.

“There was.”

He meets your eyes kindly.

“I think I’m here to never withhold comfort again.”

“And to see if the mountain can forgive.”

beats.label: Allesh-Gilliam - Father Tamsin Conversation, 1
beats.description:
He doesn’t answer immediately.

“It wants to not be extracted like an enemy.”

A gentle smile.

“You can feed a town without treating the earth like a battlefield.”

beats.label: Allesh-Gilliam - Father Tamsin Conversation, 2
beats.description:
“No.”

A pause.

“I think it’s tired.”

He meets your eyes.

“Anger is sharp. Fatigue is worse.”

beats.label: Allesh-Gilliam - Father Tamsin Conversation, 3
beats.description:
“Less noise.”

“Fewer rushed decisions.”

“More gratitude.”

beats.label: Allesh-Gilliam - Father Tamsin Conversation, 4
beats.description:
He smiles faintly.

“Because leaving is easier.”

That’s all he gives.

beats.label: Allesh_Gilliam - Inspect the Long Market

choices.label: Follow up
choices.description: on that beat ... she seems to be expecting you to ask about something.

beats.description:
A roofed strip of welded awnings runs down what used to be Main Street. Food from Lyrenn. Ore and tools from Khezek Tor. Jackalope goods pass through quietly.

Prices shift with rumors.

Everyone watches who shops where.

Approaching you, you see a matronly looking Menhirkin in an intricate robe approaching you.

Not what you expected from - Etta Bloom?

Etta Bloom smiles like she’s already forgiven you.

She adjusts a crate that doesn’t need adjusting and looks you over like inventory that hasn’t decided what shelf it belongs on.

“People are excited,” she says pleasantly. “That’s dangerous.”

She leans closer.

“Lyrenn’s acting… attentive. You’ll want to hear what the soil’s been saying.”

A beat.

“And if you’re curious about old mistakes buried nearby—well. Best to ask before someone else does.”

beats.label: Allesh-Gilliam - Etta Bloom Conversation

choices.label: What are they up to in there?
Do you have an echo story?

beats.description:
Etta watches you the way a cat watches a cupboard door that shouldn’t be moving.

She doesn’t blink.

“Ah,” she says softly. “So we’re done pretending you’re here for grain prices.”

She adjusts a ledger that was already straight.

“Fine.”

A breath.

“The bunker.”

Her smile doesn’t leave. It just… thins.

“You’ve heard it called a Vault. That’s generous. It’s a pre-Shattering containment sink. Infrastructure-grade. Not storage. Not shelter.”

She taps the table once.

“Liability.”

A beat.

“The Valhaulans are inside it.”

She says it like confirming the weather.

“They’ve been there for at least three cycles. Long enough to strip the outer access tunnels. Long enough to mount shielded plating along the shaft. Long enough to decide it’s sacred.”

Her eyes flick up to yours.

“They call it their Rightful Sacred Battle-Bassinet.”

A small shrug.

“Which tells you exactly how stable that leadership circle is.”

She leans in.

“You want proof?”

She pulls a scrap of waxed fiber from her sleeve. Presses it into your hand.

Carved sigil. Clean lines. Fresh.

“That’s a Valhaulan seal. Not decorative.”

Her voice lowers.

“It’s directional.”

She taps the edge.

“It’s facing outward.”

A silence hangs there.

“You understand what that means.”

beats.label: Allesh-Gilliam - Etta Bloom Conversation, "What are they doing in there?"
beats.description:
Etta exhales through her nose.

“They’re not excavating treasure.”

“They’re rebinding something.”

She studies your reaction carefully.

“Rumor says the original sink was designed to hold excess Spark bleed from early terraforming grids. Pre-civilization overreach. The sort of thing that melts coastlines if left unattended.”

She gestures vaguely toward the map.

“Khezek Tor’s ore veins sit on similar infrastructure. Different design, same era.”

A beat.

“And wouldn’t you know it, Khezek Tor’s had unusual containment audits in the last two seasons.”

She tilts her head.

“Valhaulan activity has been sighted in the upper tunnels there. Quiet. Technical. Not raiding.”

“That’s not their usual hymn.”

beats.label: Allesh-Gilliam - Etta Bloom Conversation, "Are they protecting it?"
beats.description:
Her smile sharpens.

“No.”

“They’re relocating blame.”

She lets that land.

“If you reverse a sink—if you reorient the seal—you don’t stop the debt.”

“You change where it manifests.”

She folds her hands.

“And if you break it outright?”

A tiny shrug.

“Then we all get to find out what three centuries of deferred Spark pressure looks like.”

beats.label: Allesh-Gilliam - Etta Bloom Conversation, "Players hesitate"
beats.description:
Etta’s tone softens—not kinder, but steadier.

“You’re not the only coalition sniffing that coastline.”

“Lyrenn wants the soil tech.”

“Khezek Tor wants the infrastructure.”

“The Jackalopes want leverage.”

“And the Valhaulans?”

She gives a short laugh.

“They want myth.”

Her gaze hardens.

“Which is worse.”

beats.label: Allesh-Gilliam - Etta Bloom Convo Exit
beats.description:
She meets your eyes.

“It’s Valhaulans. Not rumor. Not ghost markings.”

“They’re inside.”

“They’ve sealed it.”

“And whatever that sink was designed to hold?”

She straightens.

“It’s starting to hum.”

She slides the sigil back toward you.

“Restore it, and Khezek Tor keeps the burden.”

“Redirect it, and you choose who pays.”

“Break it, and no one owes anyone anything anymore.”

Her smile returns. Warm. Polite. Deadly.

“Markets love clarity.”

A pause.

“Societies rarely survive it.”

beats.label: Allesh-Gilliam - Etta Bloom Conversation, echo
beats.description:
She laughs softly.

“Oh, sweetheart.”

“You think I spun out incomplete?”

She tilts her head.

“I was a treasurer once. Pre-Shattering or post, doesn’t matter.”

“I balanced something that wasn’t meant to balance.”

Her eyes flick toward the coastline.

“I moved debt.”

A pause.

“Not money. Consequence.”

She smooths a crate edge.

“I think I’m here to watch what happens when it comes due.”

A faint smile.

“And to make sure it lands where it teaches the right lesson.”

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - Introduction
beats.description:
From the road, the place looks like a corpse that refused to lie down.

A half‑collapsed pre‑Fall factory squats in the dust, patched with sheet metal, railcar doors, and stubborn competence. Wind chimes made of shell casings and old keys clatter constantly, never quite settling.

Painted above the bay door:

Fixit and Goods

The generators are running.

So is the math.

choices.label: The Gullywasher
choices.description: There's a bar! Drunk Jackalopes could be fun. And drunk people tell tales. Do drunk Jackalopes?

choices.label: General Store
choices.description: Store = buying stuff = maybe that's where they have the Leyline Macguffin thing? Or people to give you quests? Or stuff to buy? General Stores are a magical uncollapsed reality of potential!

choices.label: Arc Bay
choices.description: Arc Bay just SOUNDS bad ass, right? And they have rigs! Maybe go and be envious? Also, good to know the kind of booze a mechanic likes, in case of emergencies, so this is a NETWORKING opportunity as well.

choices.label: Generator
choices.description: Power generator = tended by people who know about energy = Venn diagram with people whgo know about Leyline MacGuffins. Hopefully. You're new at ... judgement ...

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - The Gully Washer Exterior
beats.description:
Unimpressive. Looks in no way specially Jackalope related. How are they supposed to get this place on the map? 1 out of 10 stars would not recommend based on my knee jerk reaction.

Ok I'm over it go ahead and go in.

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - Gullywasher Conversation

choices.label: 1. Chat with the bartender
choices.description:
"Chupacabras have always been at war with Jackalopes." It is known. This is the way.

Huh. That must have been a lie?

choices.label: 2. Chat with the bartender
choices.description: "We're not Jackalopes, we come in peace!" But seriously haha what gives here?

choices.label: 3. Chat with the bartender
choices.description: If we buy stuff can we also ask you questions? That's how being a bartender is all about right? Would it help if we got drunk and complained about our shitty lives and passed out and then asked questions about local stuff? What's the protocol here?

choices.label: 4. Chat with the bartender
choices.description: We're the new folk from up the road a manifestation. Took over Allesh-Gilliam and the adjacents from the last Order contingent, now that it's established. We're trying to learn what we've gotten ourselves into. We are also in need of a Leyline stabilizer, if you happen to know where one might acquire such things?

beats.description:
There is a Chupacabra standing behind the bar, washing glasses. Oh shit he's the bartender. The Q&A person. The being worth seeing.

That was not on your post-Apocalyptic 5D bingo card this morning.

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - The Gullywasher,  Choice 1
beats.description:
Dougan pauses mid-polish.

“Ah. You’re listening to the old script.”

He sets the glass down with deliberate care.

“Yes, yes, that was the story. Claws, horns, blood in the scrublands. Very operatic. Very marketable.”

He leans in slightly.

“But one must ask — who kept staging it?”

He taps the bar twice.

“I have tasted Jackalope wine. It is mediocre, but earnest. We are not natural enemies. We were… encouraged.”

He smiles, sharp but not unkind.

“You may wish to investigate who benefits from inherited hatreds.”

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - The Gullywasher,  Choice 2
beats.description:
Dougan clasps his hands delightedly.

“Peace? In this town? Oh, how scandalous.”

He steps around the bar and adjusts one of your collars without asking.

“You must understand, most people enter expecting to confirm a story. You have entered hoping to revise one.”

He gestures toward the back shelves.

“I host poetry readings on Wednesdays. Cross-species attendance encouraged.”

He lowers his voice.

“If you truly come in peace, then stay long enough to be seen. Visibility is the first ingredient of diplomacy.”

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - The Gullywasher,  Choice 3
beats.description:
Dougan’s eyes light up.

“A patron who understands the transaction of atmosphere.”

He gestures toward the chalkboard.

“You may ask three questions with the purchase of the tasting flight.”

He slides you a small glass.

“First question is free. It is a gesture of optimism.”

Then:

“The local staff protocol? We survive by aligning with the Gate’s mood. It has been… unsettled.”

He glances toward the leyline shimmer.

“It remembers something incorrectly.”

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - The Gullywasher, Choice 4
beats.description:
Dougan listens without interruption.

When you finish, he nods slowly.

“You are not conquerors.”

He adjusts his cufflinks.

“You are… custodians of an unfinished chapter.”

He gestures toward the room.

“This saloon exists because I believe even myths deserve revision.”

Then, carefully:

“A Leyline stabilizer, you say? That is ambitious. Culture can anchor flow as effectively as iron.”

He taps the bar.

“Host something. Invite someone who should not feel welcome.”

He smiles, fanged and earnest.

“That is how you stabilize a place.”

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - The Gullywasher,  Choice 1 (Fail)
beats.description:
Dougan laughs — not mockingly, but musically.

“Oh, darling. If we were truly at war, you would not be drinking under my roof.”

He gestures to the glowing ley sigils embedded in the tables.

“War leaves scars. Culture leaves seating arrangements.”

Then, lightly:

“If you intend to interrogate me, at least order something first. I recommend the rosemary-infused radish gin.”

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - The Gullywasher,  Choice 2 (Fail)
beats.description:
Dougan studies you for a long moment.

“My dear, if you announce peace before anyone has accused you, you sound like a defendant.”

He offers a drink anyway.

“Relax. No one here intends to eat you. Not today.”

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - The Gullywasher,  Choice 3 (Fail)
beats.description:
Dougan narrows his eyes theatrically.

“I do not sell gossip. I curate ambiance.”

Beat.

“But ambiance includes rumors, and rumors occasionally fall into glasses.”

He pours you something cheap.

“You may begin.”

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - The Gullywasher, Choice 4 (Fail)
beats.description:
Dougan raises one brow.

“You have taken over territory and your first instinct is to announce it in a bar?”

He sighs dramatically.

“Power without elegance is merely noise.”

He hands you a menu.

“Try again. Slower.”

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - Power Station Exterior
beats.description:
The exterior of the Generator Hall is a testimony to the ingenuity of Jackalopes. And their contractors, I suppose. This place shouldn't work. Like - it REALLY should have killed a lot of people. In a several hundred mile radius.

Instead, it provides a community service.

Just goes to show you ... something!

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - Power Station Conversation
beats.description:
Heat hits first.

Then noise.

The Generator Hall is a cathedral of vibration.

Massive turbines spin under thick housing.

Old Gearbox moves through it like a priest in ritual space.

There are upgrades here.

Recent.

Careful.

Redundant shielding.

Additional dampeners.

Someone is preparing for load increase.

Or surge.

Or impact.

You are not allowed here unescorted.

And if you are invited, it is not casual.

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - Power Station Conversation 1
beats.description:
“Cooling vents.”

“Second sublevel still sealed.”

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - Power Station Conversation 2
beats.description:
“Generators don’t care who’s in charge.”

Beat.

“I respect that.”

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - General Store Exterior
beats.description:
This place used to be a strip mall. Or a gas station. Or strip club. Given how things used to be, it was probably all three at once.

Now it sells socks and biscuits.

And guns.

And hope.

This list NOT in order based on sales volume.

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - General Store Conversation
beats.description:
The Counter is a slab of reinforced metal worn smooth at the edges.

Drawers beneath it slide silently.

Every transaction passes here.

Parts.

Promises.

Information.

There is no price list.

There is only pause.

Mara or whoever stands here does not quote numbers.

They look at you.

And then they quote weight.

Not of currency.

Of relationship.

The Counter hums faintly.

Not electrical.

Accounting.

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - General Store Conversation 1
beats.description:
She flips coin.

“People starting things.”

Coin stops.

“Not finishing them.”

Direct eye contact.

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - General Store Conversation 2
beats.description:
She doesn’t hesitate.

“Two crates stuck in a dispute.”

“Settle it clean.”

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - General Store Conversation 3
beats.description: “I like invoices paid.”

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - Arc Bay Exterior
beats.description:

beats.label: Lyrenn - Opening Scene
beats.description:
The road to Lyrenn smells different.

Warm earth. Sap. Old rain coaxed out of stubborn ground.

Fields stretch wider than they should, given the soil, given the history, given Bad Eden’s general hostility toward optimism.

Someone made this place work anyway.

The land does not feel safe.

It feels patient.

Lyrenn is built around the reinforced shell of an old agricultural co‑op and grain elevator, braced with timber, prayer, and experience. Solar cloth hangs between poles like tired flags. Wind chimes made from irrigation parts sing constantly, keeping pests—mundane and otherwise—uneasy.

People here do not carry weapons openly.

They carry tools.

That is a choice.

It is also a risk.

The land here is responsive. Too responsive. Crops grow in patterns that suggest intention. Vines curl when spoken to kindly. Soil tightens when lied to.

Lyrenn does not punish violence immediately.

It remembers it.

beats.label: Lyrenn - Green Ring - Cinematic
beats.description:
The old grain elevator rises like a memory that refused to collapse.

Around it stretches a wide circular field — unnervingly symmetrical.

No fences divide it.

No private rows break its curve.

Planting is radial.

Harvest is radial.

Everything leads toward the elevator at the center, like spokes toward a promise.

The soil here is darker than the surrounding land.

Darker — and quieter.

You feel it before you name it:

This place listens.

A wooden platform stands at the edge of the circle.

Not a stage.

A witness stand.

When wind moves across the Ring, it does not rustle — it breathes.

choices.label: Chat with Rowan of the Loam

beats.description:
The irrigation channels run on gravity alone.

Stone-lined. Hand-carved.

When water flows, it sings.

Not metaphorically.

Notes rise where channels narrow.

Low tones hum in wider basins.

It is not music with rhythm.

It is music with patience.

Workers move slower here.

Arguments soften.

Animals drink, then leave.

But when you step close —

The tone shifts.

Just slightly.

As if something is tuning itself around you.

A child nearby whispers:

“It’s trying to figure you out.”

Quick, try something else before they use their terrifying children powers on you.

choices.label: You don’t trust the mountain either.
Do you have an echo story?
Can we see the seed vault?

beats.description:
Elsin Quade wipes her hands on her apron before offering one to you.

Her grip is firm. Callused. Honest.

“You can force food out of the land,” she says plainly.

A pause.

“Or you can listen and be fed longer.”

She does not beg for help.

She is watching to see if you notice the difference.

beats.label: Lyrenn - Chat with Elsin Quade, 1
beats.description:
She gestures to irrigation.

[annoyed] “You’re pushing expansion faster than soil rotation.”

[thoughtful] “If you want three harvests now, you lose thirty later.”

[exhales sharply] If you need short-term yields ... Then say that plainly.”

At the end of the day, I respect honesty over idealism."

beats.label: Lyrenn - Chat with Elsin Quade, 2
beats.description:
She doesn’t answer immediately.

“Fewer sudden mandates.”

“Clear planting schedules.”

“Protection from raids.”

She clearly will not say “help us” twice.

beats.label: Lyrenn - Chat with Elsin Quade, 3
beats.description:
She glances toward Tor.

“I trust cycles.”

“Not ambition.”

beats.label: Lyrenn - Chat with Elsin Quade, echo
beats.description:
She doesn’t like this question.

But she answers.

“I used to farm where soil cracked if you breathed wrong.”

“I forced yields.”

A tight nod.

“Met quota.”

Her jaw sets.

“Then the ground died.”

She looks toward Lyrenn’s fields.

“I think I’m here to learn how to ask instead.”

A beat.

“And to see if land remembers gentleness.”

beats.label: Lyrenn - Chat with Rowan of the Loam

choices.label: What happens when the Darkness spikes?
Do you have an echo story?

beats.description:
Rowan looks at you like they’re trying to remember your face from a dream that hasn’t happened yet.

“The crops know you,” they say, frowning slightly.

“That’s… new.”

They press their palm to the soil and wince.

“It’s been loud lately.”

beats.label: Lyrenn - Chat with Rowan of the Loam, 1
beats.description:
Rowan winces.

“You are.”

They press soil.

“You’re… organizing the roots.”

A small breath.

“That could be good.”

Or not.

beats.label: Lyrenn - Chat with Rowan of the Loam, 2
beats.description:
Rowan studies you.

“You’re deciding.”

This is literal.

They feel faction drift in real time.

beats.label: Lyrenn - Chat with Rowan of the Loam, 3
beats.description:
They grip their head.

“The soil tries to forget what it grew.”

beats.label: Lyrenn - Chat with Rowan of the Loam, echo
beats.description:
Rowan frowns.

“I don’t think I was someone.”

They press fingers into the dirt.

“I think I was pressure.”

A small, uncertain shrug.

“Something the soil needed to say.”

Their eyes flick to you.

“You’re loud in the roots.”

A wince.

“I’m here because something is trying to decide if you’re safe.”

beats.label: Lyrenn - Seed Vault
beats.description:
The reinforced hatch groans like it resents being opened. Almost as much as Elsin Quade resents being asked to open it, I guess. But she reluctantly agreed to your request amd now stands with now somewhat expectant eyes at you, not inside the vault.

Cold air exhales upward.

Below, shelves descend in careful rows.

Glass jars. Steel cases. Cloth-wrapped bundles.

Each labeled in meticulous script.

Pre-Fall corn.

Salt-tolerant rye.

Drought-sung barley.

A section cordoned off with simple red thread.

Inside those jars:

Seeds that hum.

Not loudly.

Not constantly.

But enough that silence feels incomplete without them.

No one has planted those in years.

No one has agreed not to.

beats.description:
You hear Khezek Tor before you see it.

A low, constant vibration—stone grinding against memory. The mine’s mouth yawns open in a cliffside that looks like it was bitten out of the world rather than excavated.

Floodlights burn day and night.

Not for visibility.

For warning.

Structures here are brutal, efficient, and unapologetic. Shipping containers welded into barracks. Cranes frozen mid‑lift like skeletons of failed gods. The air tastes metallic, sharp enough to make your tongue ache.

If Lyrenn teaches patience,

Khezek Tor teaches limits.

This place exists because it must.

And because no one else wants to pay the cost.

Yesodium is a hell of a drug.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - The Maw
beats.description:
The mouth of the shaft is wider than comfort requires.

Timbers creak. Metal groans.

Cold air climbs upward like breath from a sleeping animal.

The primary shaft descends deeper than the original survey maps ever dared to suggest.

Level markers hang crooked.

Level Four is scratched over twice.

Below that, no official numbering exists.

The walls are veined with faintly glowing ore.

Not bright.

Not constant.

More like pulse memory caught mid-thought.

When the mine rests, whispers rise.

Not words.

Contours of thought.

As if the stone is rehearsing something it hasn’t decided to become.

No one goes below Level Four alone anymore.

Not after the leaning started.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - The Lift Hall
beats.description:
The Lift Hall never stops moving.

Chains rattle.

Platforms rise and fall.

Ore carts roll in endless procession.

Rig components are staged in ordered stacks — pristine beside raw stone.

Workers rotate fast.

Faces blur.

Authority underground is simple:

Someone decides.

Or everyone dies.

The air tastes metallic and electric.

Not from tools.

From possibility.

Yesodium shipments are marked carefully.

Handled with gloves.

Spoken to, sometimes.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - The Brace
beats.description:
A massive reinforcement structure groans under its own ambition.

Iron struts layered over timber.

Stone plugs wedged against collapse.

The Brace holds back a section that already fell once.

Chalk marks cover every beam.

Measurements. Angles. Names.

Warning sigils overlap older warnings.

And sometimes —

When the mine is quiet —

The Brace shifts.

Not enough to fall.

Enough to remind everyone it could.

If it fails, the mountain will not simply collapse.

The hex will change.

Permanently.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - Drax Calder Convo

choices.label: You afraid of something down there?
Do you have an echo story?

beats.description:
Drax Calder doesn’t waste time shaking hands.

He gestures toward the mine instead.

“The mountain doesn’t hate us,” he says flatly.

A pause. Something shifts behind the Brace.

“It’s just tired of being hollowed out.”

He looks at you—not to intimidate, but to measure.

“You want results? Fine. Just don’t pretend this is clean work.”

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - Drax Calder Convo, 1
beats.description:
He doesn’t answer directly.

“Deep enough that maps stop mattering.”

He watches your reaction to uncertainty.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - Drax Calder Convo, 2
beats.description:
"No.”

A beat.

“I’m wary.”

“Fear panics. Wariness measures.”

He respects that distinction.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - Drax Calder Convo, 3
beats.description:
Silence.

“That’s the question.”

He’s never heard someone ask it.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - Drax Calder Convo, echo
beats.description:
He answers bluntly.

“I chased a vein once.”

“No safety. No surveys.”

“It collapsed.”

A silence.

“Men under it.”

He doesn’t look away.

“I’m here to finish digging the right way.”

A beat.

“Or to know when to stop.”

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - Sable Nine convo

choices.label: Are we part of the anomaly?
Do you have an echo story?

beats.description:
Sable Nine keeps their maps folded like secrets.

“I chart what moves,” they say quietly. “Not what’s supposed to.”

They tap a point on the map that refuses to stay still.

“The mine rearranges itself when it thinks no one’s watching.”

A beat.

“I’ve seen something lean back.”

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - Sable Nine convo, 1
beats.description:
“Something that noticed the noticing.”

Your cklear confusion seems to relax him.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - Sable Nine convo, 2
beats.description:
Because pretending they’re normal is lethal.”

They glance toward the gate.

“You can survive unpredictability. Not denial.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - Sable Nine convo, 3
beats.description:
A long look.

“Yes.”

But not accusatory.

Khezek-Tor - Sable Nine convo, echo
beats.description:
Sable studies the map while speaking.

“I used to predict things.”

“Markets. Storms. Shifts.”

A faint tension in their voice.

“I missed one.”

They tap the map where it shifts.

“It cost people.”

A breath.

“I think I’m here to catch what moves before it pretends it’s still.”

They glance up.

“And to say ‘I don’t know’ before someone dies.”

choices.label: Justice
choices.description: Tough but fair. Very frontier. Let the little guy pay off his debts. The law has other ways of dealing with hunger and want, besides stealing.

choices.label: Punish
choices.description: Examples are awesome. This is a harsh place. The social contract is incredibly important here. Make a mistake and other people don't get second chances. Why should it be any different here.

beats.description:
The thief is moved to a back room.

Hands still bound.

Bleeding, but not gravely.

The Jackalopes aren’t angry.

They’re quiet.

Mara gestures lightly.

“This is your territory.”

“What does justice look like?”

The thief says:

“It wasn’t for me.”

That might be true.

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - Punish the Prisoner
beats.description:
Miliard stands up, lets himself out of his bonds, and says "Well at least now we know. Don't piss these people off. Yeesh. I hope we didn't just piss them off MORE. Mara, was the PipnPatter's idea? You could have gotten me seriously punished. Dougan now owes me five beers for putting myself in harm's way for the good of our enclave. Good day!" And he scurries out the door.

Mara says "Thank you. We had to know. Don't blame us for the trickery. It's in our nature. We're wascawy."

And with that she, somewhat petulantly, HOPS out of the Arc Bay.

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - Justice for the Prisoner
beats.description:
Miliard stands up, lets himself out of his bonds, and says "Well at least now we know. Tough but fair. I personally prefer a BIT more flexibility, but I can live with it. Willing to wager the rest of us can too ... Dougan now owes me five beers for putting myself in harm's way for the good of our enclave. Good day!" And he scurries out the door.

Mara smiles faintly, and says "Thank you. We had to know. Don't blame us for the trickery. It's in our nature. We're wascawy."

And with that she, somewhat smugly, HOPS out of the Arc Bay.

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - Mercy for the Prisoner
beats.description:
Miliard stands up, lets himself out of his bonds, and says "Well then. Smart, compassionate, cute - everything we want in our new leaders. Dougan now owes me five beers for putting on such an amazing performance for the good of our enclave. Good day!" And he scurries out the door.

Mara grins broadly says "Thank you. We had to know. Don't blame us for the trickery. It's in our nature. We're wascawy. And that's how we show affection. By sometimes shooting you in the face with a shotgun."

And with a laugh and a snort, she somewhat giddily HOPS out of the Arc Bay.

Furrier's Fixit Farm - The Prisoner is not our problem
beats.description:
When you turn green from the pressure, Mara quickly says "I'm so sorry, this was a test. Miliard is fine. We just wanted to see what you would do. And you freaked the fuck out. So now we know."

Miliard stands up, removes his bonds, bows, and says "My ability to churn the stomachs of mortals with my performances is one of my greatest gifts. Do not take it too hard, my timid friends. I have been told that I am a LOT!" And with that he scurries out.

Mara turns to leave, and then stops, sighs, turns slowly back around, and says "Piece of advice new bosses. This ain't a place for waffling. You don't make decisions, decisions get made for you, sometimes a split second later. That's a freebie."

And she leaves.

Young Gearbox shrugs and goes back to work.

Small root-burrowers — pale, soft-bodied things — tear irrigation channels apart.

Might as well show them what you do to things who try to take what's yours; things that burn, and things that fall easily to the axe.

I realize now that this could apply to many different things, which greatly reduces the emotional impact of the above statement.

God. Dammit.

choices.label: Do nothing
choices.description: Lyrenn has a LOT of shit going wrong with it huh? Must really suck to live here ... Someone should probably do something about it or something.

Paths you walked yesterday bend elsewhere.

Clearings reopen in apology.

Branches lean inward as you speak.

Wind carries tone, not words.

When someone raises their voice, birds scatter.

When someone softens, roots uncoil slightly.

The forest is not aggressive.

But they are ALSO full of a pretty awesome magical sap, which they are willing to share.

So, like, win win!

beats.description: Have you ever seen a forest arguing about who gets to have the window seat? It's quite a thing to behold. But you got the trees to the right place, and Lyrenn is breathing much easier. Hope whoever lives near there likes asshole trees!

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - The Mine That Answered Back, Quest Acceptance
Khezek-Tor - The Mine that answered back

choices.label: Exploit it
choices.description: Yesodium is SUPER useful. NOT continuing would be really stupid. Bad leadership really. Drill baby drill!!!

choices.label: Seal the Breach
choices.description:
Shut that shit DOWN. I'm pretty sure I read somewhere that delving too deeply was BAD.

Options - 

2 OP (any type)

Valuable material

Public vow

choices.label: Open it up fully
choices.description:
Fuck it. Dynamite this bitch. There has to be more magical silence Yesodium shit close by!! It is all be yours!

4 Violence OPs

beats.description:
The new shaft broke into silence.

Not cavern.

Not creature.

Silence.

Tools vibrate in hands before striking.

Rock leans inward.

Miners dream of owing something.

Of signing contracts they do not remember reading.

The ore veins rearrange subtly overnight.

Not randomly.

Like something adjusting posture.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - The Mine that answered back, seal
beats.description:
Like most things in Bad Eden, sealing the breach comes with a cost.

To achieve this goal, you must spend 2 OP (Faction Choice)

The seal stabilizes, which lessens the eldritch energies flowing into the mine. 

Yesodium output reduced slightly, reducing Economy OP by 1 this turn.

But the mine no longer rumbles ominously. The mountain seems more ... at ease.

Khezek-Tor gains the Well Fortified condition.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - The Mine that answered back, exploit
beats.description:
You double your Economy OP bank. This is a massive production effort.

You are, in fact, able to use some of the extra output to add additional stability to the Allesh-Gilliam Leygate

Darkness increases by 3. 

The Brace is now one narrative step closer to collapse.

Khezek-Tor now has a hostile population as a mysterious illness sweeps through the compound.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - The Mine that answered back, open
beats.description:
Well. This containment sink is no longer containing anything. 

It's quiet at the moment. But you have an open Qlipothic energy sink, that is now slowly morphing into a portal.

+2 darkness ... and maybe rising.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - The Shipment of Utter Darkness Sometimes
Khezek-Tor - The Shipment of Utter Darkness sometimes

choices.label: Standardize
choices.description: Ok, you're starting to get the vibe here. Things are haphazard. They don't have processes. There workflow is suboptimal. They don't have enough stories on their scrum board. The ore doesn't feel valued properly. You can help with this!

choices.label: Rite
choices.description: You think you can see just enough of the problem to nudge it out of the way with a properly formulated rite. A way to communicate directly with the stone, thank it, and frame operations here properly.

choices.label: Ignore
choices.description: It's still ore, ain't it? Maybe if we just harvest MORE of it, we'll get through the tainted bits!

beats.description:
Ore crates from Khezek-Tor hum faintly during transit.

Not ominous.

Unsettled.

When mishandled, arguments erupt nearby.

Lights flicker.

Dreams sour.

The ore isn’t cursed.

It’s improperly framed.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - The Shipment of Utter Darkness sometimes, standardize
beats.description:
You implement a standard sacred handling protocol. 

This slows down your transportation, giving you time to add proper markings and orientation to the shipments.

This costs 3 Economy OP.

And raises morale by 2.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - The Shipment of Utter Darkness sometimes, rite
beats.description:
You perform a simple rite of orientation and atonement for the stone. It may or may not have involved puppets. The rock has a surprisingly short attention span for a tectonically oriented sentience. But it got the vibe, and understands the goals here.

People are impressed. Word spreads - damn elegant solution, that. Someone who gets mines. 

You made some allies today.

+2 to Morale and Loyalty, -1 to Darkness, +2 to non lethal, soft power, culture, and faith OP banks.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - The Shipment of Utter Darkness sometimes, ignore
beats.description:
The tainted shipments continue. Some folks get sick. The mood in your enclaves dampens a bit.

But the Economy does seem to be getting better.

+2 Economy OPs. -1 morale, +1 darkness

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - The Valhaulan Seal, Quest Acceptance
Khezek-Tor - Valhaulan Seal Cinematic
beats.description:
The sealed shaft bears Valhaulan sigils.

Recent.

Precise.

Directional.

The seal doesn’t bind inward.

It points outward.

Like a pipe.

Like a siphon.

choices.label: Restore the seal
choices.description: As best you can figure, the Valhaulans have weaponized the Yeodium's resentment. Then, it was resentment about being left untapped and in potentia. Someone, somewhere, is getting a blast of bad juju. Best reclaim what's yours. And then have a long talk with some Valhaulans.

choices.label: Redirect the seal's energies
choices.description: At least this way you KNOW where you're sending the bad vibes? Hit a hex that you hope isn't populated? That way Khezek-Tor doesn't get hit with all of that bad juju coming back home. That would seriously slow down production.

choices.label: Break the seal
choices.description: What did they seal up to get this thing humming to begin with? Dynamite this mutha! Open it up! let's see what's inside!!

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - The Valhaulan Seal, restore
beats.description:
Khezek-Tor becomes Irradiated for one turn due to the massive re-ingestion of the outsourced energies.

Turns out there was a Valhaulan Sympathizer group in town. They got pissed, made some noise, got collared. That could cause problems later. 

Yesodium mining actually runs steady, so no economic impact.

And you have clearly shown what kind of outfit you are trying to run here.

-2 to darkness. -1 to morale.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - The Valhaulan Seal, redirect
beats.description:
You can feel a brief intake of psychic breath, like the fetid breeze off a swamp, as the seal recalls its burden and then redirects it towards your newly chosen target.

The entire region knows you did this.

They worry you might do it again.

They worry it might be them next.

-2 morale, loyalty, +2 darkness

-1 step to relationship with all Faction with whom one is not already Friendly.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - The Valhaulan Seal, break
beats.description:
That was unwise, you say to yourself and anyone else who will listen approximately .5 picoseconds after the seal crumbles.

This kills all the PCs and renders Khezek Tor a wasteland hex.

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - The Leyline Stabilizer
beats.description:
The Leygate hums like someone pretending they aren’t tired.

Blue flickers yellow.

Yellow flickers blue.

The stabilizer readout shows turbulence.

Not failure.

Persistence.

Avuncular Joan’s key still functions.

One charge remains.

The engineer doesn’t look relieved.

“That’s worse.”

If it misfires, it won’t explode.

It will remember wrong.

“Send the wrong shape of thing.”

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - Leyline Stabilizer Negotiation

choices.label: Trade
choices.description:
Pretty sure that you can come to some sort of equitable trading set up. This is their gig. They just want to know who they're dealing with, and if you've come and presented yourselves as you are, or as you might be, or as you were.

Make a persuasion check or spend 2 Soft Power OP.

choices.label: Shared Oversight
choices.description: You know, you ARE new here. There is a working Leygate here at Fixit Farm - they know what they're doing. Setting up a network would be nice. Cozy. Neighborly. Convenient. What about shared oversight of the network?

choices.label: Hard Ask
choices.description: Time to show folks around here that compliance and cooperation with your faction are not optional. They will give it to you. And be thankful that you do not ask for more. Ok you don't SAY that second part out loud, but you say it with your eyes. Actually you find out later that someone was holding up a sign saying it. But right now you don't know that.

choices.label: Delay
choices.description: Why is everyone staring at you? This is fucked up. A lot of pressure right here. Get this wrong and you'll never be able to make a first impression again. Better pretend you mispronounced what you want and actually meant something else and you will check back later.

beats.description:
Mara clicks her thumb in anticipation. "Now this is what we're about. 

What you got as we might want?"

And then she tries REALLY hard to not look interested but instead looks like she's trying really hard to not look interested but is failing badly but doesn't know that she's failing badly.

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - Leyline Stabilizer - Trade
beats.description:
You conclude your negotiation with a handshake.

You have secured assurances that the Jackalopes will send someone along with the stabilizer who will install it.

You feel, for the first time since arriving in Bad Eden really, not quite entirely unlike a competent person.

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - Leyline Stabilizer - Shared Oversight
beats.description:
You conclude your negotiation with a handshake, and a shot of some harsh orange liquid that tastes strongly of petrichor and fucks you up stright and proper.

You have secured assurances that the Jackalopes will send someone along with the stabilizer who will install it, and help your engineering team get it up and running and calibrated.

You feel, for the first time since arriving in Bad Eden really, slightly competent.

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - Leyline Stabilizer - Hard Ask
beats.description:
You firmly explain that the entire region needs this, and will benefit from your ability to easily move about your new command. They don't argue, just quietly nod and load the component up on a sledge for you to use to transport it home.

Everyone seems to lose interest in you at that point, although people are still quite polite.

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - Leyline Stabilizer - Delay
beats.description:
"Well - ok then," says Mara, with a quaver in her voice that is both amused and nervous.

"We'll have it whenever you're ready to talk to us about equipment. If you need us to explain anything to you, let us know. Hope you ... well, ok then!"

And Mara heads back out.

Young Gearbox has a puzzled look on his face - but simply shrugs and continues his work.

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - Leyline Stabilizer - No Deal
beats.description:
Mara lifts an eyebrow - in surprise, disgust, or as the result of an uncontrolled muscle spasm, you're not sure.

"Uh, no deal. What else ya got?"

beats.label: Acid Bog
beats.description:
The air around you grows suddenly caustic.

Then you notice the water around you starting to bubble, and hiss, and steam. 

The vines draped across the road begin to pulse like giant straws, feeding from the acid - hopefully soon to feed on disintegrated Cocky Ass Factions who think they don't need to read up on local flora-based traps.

Maybe being liquified and eaten will teach you to be more aware.

You woke up an Acid Bog(gart).

choices.label: Make a run for it
choices.description: Hold your breath, cover your face with a magazine and something, and hope you still have skin on the other side.

choices.label: Look for another way around
choices.description: Back it up. Ask for directions if you have to. Acid Boggarts are bad news, especially if you don't have a rig to shield you.

choices.label: Disperse the fumes
choices.description:
You are very resourceful. Otherwise you wouldn't be here.

That's what you tell yourself.

Time to prove it!

Come up with an ingenious way of keeping the fumes away from your sensitive pink/yellow/lime green parts!

beats.label: Acid Bog - Successful run
beats.description:
Holy shitfuck. That worked ... I mean ...

I ALWAYS BELIEVED IN YOU GUYS!

That's one for the record books ...

In which it will be said that you immediately charged the Acid Boggart and overcame it with sheer will alone!

And lots of drugs because that makes the story more interesting.

beats.label: Acid Bog - fail run
beats.description:
Well. It's good to experience defeat and death often. Builds character and strength and calluses on the parts that are repeatedly hack off or melted or what have you.

Back to it!

beats.label: Acid Bog - logistics success
beats.description:
Those very kind Wendigos took time out of their busy schedule warping space and time and the souls of others to give you directions around the Acid Boggart. That was  awful nice of them.

There was something off about them though ...

beats.label: Acid Bog - logistics failure
beats.description:
Those dick Wendigos wouldn't even take time out of their busy schedule warping space and time and the souls of others to give you directions around the Acid Boggart. What bitches.

And those are the only locals you could find. Uh, maybe try something else.

beats.label: Acid Bog - intrigue success
beats.description:
What an AMAZING idea you had! I really like the part where <...>! And then when <...> TOTALLY <...>

Classic <...>

Onwards and upwards!

beats.label: Acid Bog - intrigue failure
beats.description:
Well, back to the drawing b ... nope, the drawing board has fallen into the acid.

Figure something else out!

beats.label: Forest of Early Tifaret - Approach
beats.description:
The forest opens the way the mouth of a priest opens:

Slowly. Reverently. With absolute certainty that you are meant to be here.

The author IMMEDIATELY REGRETS the above analogy. But it's too late, so there you are.

Light spills between the trunks in deliberate beams, like an apology practiced in advance. Leaves hum—not sound exactly, more like agreement. The air tastes green and electric.

This place is beautiful in the way a knife is beautiful.

Polished. Purposeful. Waiting.

This forest believes harmony is achievable.

Not aspirationally.

Correctly.

The trees grow at ideal distances. The paths curve just enough to feel intentional. Wildlife watches without fear. Nothing here lunges. Nothing flees.

Every branch angles itself toward balance.

The forest does not want you dead.

It wants you better.

That is not the same thing as wanting you safe.

beats.label: Forest of Early Tifaret - Merge and Learn

choices.label: Soft Power
choices.description: Reach out with a spirit of compassion and grace.

choices.label: Diplomacy
choices.description: Reach out with feelings of openness, of sharing.

choices.label: Faith
choices.description: Open yourself to the clearly spiritual experience that is happening all around you. You don't need to understand to benefit.

choices.label: Nonlethal
choices.description: Reach out with a spirit of peace and calm. Be still in the middle of the energies that swirl around you.

beats.label: Forest of Tifaret - Cleanse the Forest
beats.description:
“You don’t get to decide what we become.”

Roots pull back. Light concentrates. The ground tightens like a fist.

An Aggressive Tiferet Tree Person emerges to give you what you clearly want. A fight.

beats.label: Forest of Tifaret - Leave

choices.label: Logistics
choices.description: Try and work out the path of least resistance - with reach of the fewest grasping branches and root clusters - and the right angle to tap a weak spot in a wall that you noticed, (a solid thwak with a rock will do it, which is trivial), which will cause it to drop some mortar on the tree, distracting it while you make your hurried escape.

choices.label: Intrigue
choices.description: Look over there, it's Tree Elvis! NO I SWEAR LOOK! KEEP LOOKING! THAT'S IT! WATCH FOR THE SEQUINS. YESOD SPUN HIM OUT IN HIS JUMPSUIT PHASE THIS TIME!!"

choices.label: Diplomacy
choices.description: Look, we get what you're trying to do, and we appreciate it. And what you're talking about - mental health - is very important. But I don't feel comfortable with this set and setting. I am not trying to offend you, but I would like to recuse myself from this situation.

beats.description:
Nope. Not happening. You do not have enough spoons left today to deal with an enchanted forest asking about relationships with your mom, or dog, or ... whatever.

Time to leave!

Oh, huh, looks like the forest is co-dependent. And has other ideas ...

Uhhh ...

beats.label: Forest of Tifaret - You lose, even if you win
beats.description:
This was not a thing to be settled by violence. ESPECIALLY this. Listen. Understand. Think. Fight only when you must, and accept the darkness that you will cause.

This action caused far more darkness still.

beats.label: Forest of Tifaret - We learned something today!
beats.description:
The manic edge to the forest ... lessens. Relaxes. Feels seen. Feels valuable. And somewhere, very important and impactful things happen.

The land is glad you're here.

beats.label: Forest of Early Tifaret - Could we have learned something today?
beats.description:
The rustling of the trees fades into the distance as you  leave the strange, wise, but needy arboreal encounter behind you.

Still, you woonder if you could have helped.

And you wonder what will happen to the next group to wander close.

beats.label: Apex Predator
beats.description:
If you had a license plate, it would be in this thing's teeth. If you had a glass of water, it would have ominous rings on its surface.

Not for any particular reason, simply because I find these images compelling.

Here, fight it!

beats.label: Apex Predator - Win
beats.description:
So these are things that run around on your land. You don't even know what to do about that. That can't be a good thing, right? But in Bad Eden, violence against the non-Qlipothic is almost worse than the thing you just fought.

Stewardship is hard. They don't tell you about apex predators on your land in stewardship school.

beats.label: Apex Predator - Run
beats.description: No shame. That thing was capital F ugly. And hungry. And impatient and RUDE. Throw it some tech to play with and skedaddle! Go go go!

beats.label: Apex Predator - Lose
beats.description: Hello. If I'm reading this you are probably dead. Please make your way to your designated reincarnation station to resume your adventures in Bad Eden!

beats.label: Bandit Ambush
beats.description:
"Wow. You know," you say, "This would be a great place for an ambush ..." 

In the silence, from behind one of the glowing towers, a panicked voice mutters "Wait how did they know? Who told them?"

Ah.

Here we go.

beats.label: Bandit Ambush - Run
beats.description:
Really?

Man low level D&D is so difficult to gauge. 

Was it really that bad?

Ok, good feedback.

beats.label: Bandit Ambush - Lose
beats.description:
REALLY?

Man low level D&D is so difficult to gauge. Y'all need to learn to run. That's always an option.

Anyway, reincarnate and next time use more, I dunno, techniques or something.

beats.label: Geometry Serpent
beats.description:
The ground suddenly erupts, and shatters in front of you - or rather, unfurls in front of you in an incredibly disconcerting way, leaving a shimmering canyon.

Then from within, IT unfurls something even MORE worrisome - a giant serpent composed of impossible angles and resentment for the Unproven.

beats.description:
The serpent retreats back into a dimension where you cannot follow, vanquished. 

You wipe the incomplete proofs and half solved equations off you clothes as best you can, and carry on.

beats.description: If I am reading this, you are dead. The math was too complicated. Better luck next time!

beats.label: Geometry Serpent (Run)
beats.description:
I hated my math teacher too. We used to pretend they were a zombie, because of how cold they kept the room.

Anyway no shame in cutting class.

choices.label: Power through
choices.description: Eventually this will work. Eventually this WON'T kill you and WILL give you a cool power. I mean, the law of averages right? Because causality is so reliable these days ...

beats.description:
As you travel through a patch of wood, you feel prickles on the back of ... well ... whatever you have that is prickle-able, I suppose ... and realize, you are being stal - NOPE you're being full on attacked.

By monsters.

The crashing of the underbrush alerts you before they burst into view. Some Waste Stalkers would like to see you about being savaged, torn apart, and then eaten.

Through the wisdom imparted by your amazing wilderness survival style type skills, (correspondence course edition, still lacking modules 3-5), you deduce that it's just a little rain and that never hurt anyone. Just keep going!

An apparently, since you haven't studied acid rain or octarine lightning, they can't affect you!

There was something off about them though ...

Let's get you poor dears reincarnated.

beats.description:
Pip and Patter are never late.

They don’t get lost.
They don’t miss check-ins.

So when one of them doesn’t return from a routine run, nobody panics.

They just… stop smiling.

The Jackalopes don’t make a big announcement. Word spreads sideways. The generators keep running. The Exchange stays open. But every door sounds louder when it closes.

Mara sends a message to you, terse as always.

“I don’t need heroes,” she says.
“I need to know if I should start grieving or start sharpening.”

beats.description:
The earth does not shake.

It slides.

The horizon shears sideways like a badly aligned interface. Roads drift out of agreement with themselves. Fence lines kink. A creek now insists it was always over there.

You feel it—not as fear, but as resistance.

The land is correcting a long‑standing error.

Unfortunately, you are standing in the way.

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - Approach
beats.description:
A concrete structure rises from the hill, half‑collapsed but still humming with blue light.

Broken drone parts litter the ground. A hologram flickers at the doorway, endlessly repeating:

“WELCOME TO BASIC TACTICAL INST— … error.”

The light stays on.

It thinks someone is still learning.

beats.description:
So the battle of wits has begun. To be honest, it seems a little eager. I guess it doesn't get to do this that often anymore. What with most people being dead and things.

Look, it's humming encouragingly! It WANTS you to succeed!

It will, of course, still terminate you with extreme prejudice shouild you fail, but that goes without saying, eh?

beats.description:
The entry hall smells like dust and old confidence.

Braided cables and glowing sigils form instructional diagrams along the walls. A speaker crackles:

“STATE YOUR BUSINESS OR GO AWAY.”

The system pauses.

“…OR PROCEED WITH ASSESSMENT ... ?” it asks almost desperately.

The Vault is not hostile.

It is perpetually disappointed. And lonely.

beats.label: Gloomgill - Intro
beats.description:
Before there were cities that thought themselves clever, before laws learned to wear robes and crowns, there was Oannes.

He came from the sea.

Not in conquest.
Not in fire.
But in instruction.

He rose from the water draped in scales and silence, half-man and half-fish, and he taught. Writing. Counting. Measuring. Building things that stayed built. He taught people how not to starve in predictable ways. How to argue without immediately killing one another. How to remember yesterday long enough to improve tomorrow.

Then, when the sun set, he went back into the sea.

Every day, for years.

No temples demanded.
No sacrifices required.
Just pay attention.

And people did—at first.

They wrote some of it down. They remembered pieces. They built cities and called themselves advanced. They forgot the parts that were inconvenient. They weaponized the rest. They decided they were done learning.

Oannes waited.

Centuries passed. Empires rose, fell, and rebranded their failures. The oceans swallowed coastlines. Names changed. Memory thinned. The lessons became myths, then metaphors, then trivia.

Eventually, Oannes came back up.

He looked around.
Listened.
Checked the math.

And realized—with a quiet, ancient horror—that almost no one had actually learned the important parts.

So he stopped being a teacher.

Now he is Gloomgill.

Because if you’re going to spend eternity checking the homework of history, you might as well pick a name that sounds like a problem.

Gloomgill no longer lectures. He quizzes.

He appears where people are confident and wrong. Where groups believe themselves righteous, clever, or justified. He asks questions that should have answers—about balance, consequence, cooperation, stewardship, restraint. The questions are simple. The implications are not.

Correct answers earn grudging approval.
Incorrect answers earn follow-up questions.
Repeated failure earns attention.

He does not destroy civilizations. He has tried that. It doesn’t stick.

Instead, Gloomgill harasses them.

Relentlessly. Patiently. With the Stress of a being who once believed education was enough.

Some still call him a god.
Some call him a monster.
He prefers neither.

He is not here to be worshipped.

He is here to find out whether anyone, anywhere, finally understood the lesson.

And if not—

Well.

He has all the time in the world to ask again.

beats.label: Gloomgill - intro scene
beats.description:
The marsh gives you a warning in the only language it has:

Silence.

No birds. No insects. No ripple of life. Just the thick, humid stillness of a place that has learned not to announce itself.

The water bulges.

And then Gloomgill rises—slowly, deliberately—like a debt returning with interest.

And he has a … microphone … ?

beats.label: Gloomgill - Question 1
beats.description:
“Alright contestants! First question—nice and easy!”

“Who wins if you’re right? Who benefits if you're right?"

beats.label: Gloomgill - Question 2
beats.description:
“Ooooh, judges love this one!”

“What did you break that wasn’t even playing? What did you destroy that did not oppose you?"

beats.label: Gloomgill - Question 3
beats.description:
“Lightning round!”

“If everyone did exactly what you did… what snaps first? If everyone copied you, what breaks first?"

beats.label: Gloomgill - Question 4
beats.description:
“Now thinking long-term — our sponsors love foresight!”

“Who pays for this later?”

beats.label: Gloomgill - Question 5
beats.description:
“Tricky one! Crowd favorite!”

“What problem did you skip instead of solving? Or, what problem did you AVOID solving?"

beats.label: Gloomgill - Question 6
beats.description:
“Control question! Very important!”

“Who gets to decide when this stops? When it ends?”

beats.label: Gloomgill - Question 7
beats.description:
“Ohhh, I love this one.”

“What would convince you that you’re wrong?”

beats.label: Gloomgill - Question 8
beats.description:
“Audience participation!”

“Who are you protecting—and from whom?”

beats.label: Gloomgill - Question 9
beats.description:
“Educational programming segment!”

“What lesson did you just teach everyone watching?”

beats.label: Gloomgill - Question 10
beats.description:
“Final question! No pressure!”

“If you vanish tomorrow, what’s still standing? If you disappear tomorrow, what remains?"

beats.description:
Ah, the Polygonal Forests of Bad Eden. If Bad Eden HAD tourist attractions, rather than, say, the equivalent of tourist abattoirs, this would certainly be one of them.

Is what the advert pamphlet would say.

Also, hey, looks like there's some sort of door here in the side of a hill.

The trees still manage to be more interesting, somehow.

beats.label: The Locals
beats.description: Not far from the Door in the Hill, you spot an encampment containing people who are trying and failing to give the impression that they have not yet seen you. You can tell this because of the intermittent pointing, then shushing, then brief silence, then whispered arguments. Then pointing again.

beats.label: Hidden Vault, Get To Know The Locals
beats.description:
The locals - Karsden, Menhirkin Dreamwalker; Indwimeir, Ember Touched Cosmic Linguist; Fendeddiir, Qliph-Scarred Titanbound; Sox, Felid Phantom Courier - are part of a multi generational cult, dedicated to preserving the Wonder of Cinema. 

They carry out yearly rituals such as "Night of the Premier,""The Red Carpet March,""The Sacrifice of the Papparazzi," and "The Solemn Removal of Chewing Gum." 

They await the coming of the 300th Customer, to award them The Prize - the incantation that will open the Vault and bring tbe Era of the Holy Wood to fruition.

beats.label: Warnings and Riddles
beats.description:
Your new friends have now ended their families' centuries long vigil, and in a ritual Recognition of Your Support As The 300th Customer, they empower you with the answer to the cryptic phrase, "BSTMOVIE1984," that the door repeats. 

The proper incantive response, handed down from generation to generation, is "GHSTBSTRZ." And at the end, almost reluctantly, you are handed the Ticket, a worn slip of plastic labeled "Admit One Plus Guest. No radiation zombie parking available." 

The wisdom of the ancients indeed!

worldEffects.warLog: The locals of the Hidden Vault grove offer aid and warnings.

beats.label: Uneasy Directions
beats.description: The Attendants reluctantly acknowledge that you are not The 300th Customer. You will not be shown To Your Seats. There will be no Concessions made. Please, no talking.

beats.label: Violence in the Grove
beats.description: It shouldn't have come to this. And yet, somehow, it has. You are fighting multi-generational cult families in silly hats and vests. Beware the magic of cinema!

worldEffects.warLog: The Hidden Vault approach descends into hostility.

beats.label: The Vault Door
beats.description: A sealed blast door hums with old circuitry and worse intentions. A screen flashes a message, "BSTMOVIE1984," repeatedly. It appears to be waiting for you to do something.

beats.label: The Theater
beats.description:
Empty rows. Dead screens. The smell of butter that somehow never left. The echoing sounds of cheers just out of earshot. This was a movie theater. In a bunker. A dedicated bunker for a movie theater.

Sometimes you really get why Adam did what it did ...

beats.label: The Popcorn Council
beats.description:
The room full of arguing popcorn machines goes suddenly quiet, the sound broken only by the squeaking of wheels as they all turn to look at you.

That sounds weird to say out loud.

beats.label: The Hidden Vault - The Popcorn Council, Deliberations
beats.description:
The Popcorn Council was begun at the time of The Shattering, when the two machines located here became sentient, and replicated themselves - and now await the time of The Grand Opening, when corn and butter and fun will once again ring throughout the halls - and Gilbert no longer runs the place with his ridiculous lists of demands, and trivia quizzes, amd personality tests.

And their friend the Matter Replicator might be able to make somethinb besides corn and butter and salt and coconut oil. It REALLY wants to try its hand at classical painting.

beats.label: Custodians of Sustenance
beats.description:
You have come to a mutually beneficial agreement with The Council of GenPop! You get rid of Gilbert. They make popcorn for YOU. Think of the possibilities!

Seriously, popcorn as a great carb to fiber ratio. Use grassfed butter and it's practically a superfood.

What? I want my heroes to think about their nutrition.

Do it. Or I add a Nutrition pressure bar to the Faction Sheet.

worldEffects.warLog: The Popcorn Council becomes cooperative.

beats.label: A Warning, Sort Of
beats.description: You just kind of got blown off by appliances. At least you learned that someone named Gilbert freaks these things out. Maybe they'll have better info. Or at least less paranoia.

beats.label: Silenced Concessions
beats.description:
The machines go silent, and the bunker grows meaner. You've pissed off the ancient council of appliances. No popcorn for you.

The popcorn was probably full of worms or something. Why are there so many ancient councils around here anyway??

Whatever.

worldEffects.warLog: Hostility toward the Popcorn Council destabilizes the Hidden Vault.

An ancient fabrication unit capable of infinite disappointment and finite ingredients, Lars von Replicator hums to itself - "Thalo Blue, Burnt Sienna, Lizard Skin Crimson, Titanium White." 

It seems to be printing out ... a painting?
